text:
sara_sales: Alex (customer) reporting a POC connectivity problem when the app inside their VPC talks to our Private Endpoint. Error: TLS handshake times out or the client fails verification. Can net/sec help triage? cc @eli_neteng @reza_security

alex_customer: Getting mixed results from different hosts. Example from app host A:
```
curl: (60) SSL: certificate verification failed
```
From host B it sometimes connects but returns an HTML login page. Very inconsistent. POC/demo next Tue so this is urgent.

eli_neteng: Sounds like a transparent proxy or captive portal in front of the path. Two quick checks: 1) DNS resolution for the private hostname, 2) TLS ServerHello certificate. Please run these and paste outputs:
`dig +short redwood-poc.private.example.internal @169.254.169.253`
`openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -showcerts -servername redwood-poc.redwood.internal`

alex_customer: dig -> `10.5.200.7` (internal appliance). openssl shows cert CN=appliance.login.local and a redirect to `/login`. Snippet:
```
subject=/CN=appliance.login.local
issuer=/CN=corp-root-ca
---
No client certificate CA names sent
```
Also traceroute shows hops immediately going to the appliance IP.

reza_security: If they're seeing a management/login page cert, that's definitely TLS inspection or HTTP interception. From a security questionnaire POV, we need assurance that the appliance will not persist or log auth tokens. Please ask customer to confirm appliance config (TLS passthrough for service FQDN) and whether the appliance substitutes certs (MITM).

mikael_support: Quick mitigation ideas:
- Can they add an internal DNS override for the POC that resolves to our test ENI IP (we can create one for demo traffic)? This avoids the appliance entirely.
- If override not possible, ask the infra team to whitelist redwood host in the proxy to disable TLS inspection for that hostname.
- As last resort, we can provision a temp public endpoint behind an IP allowlist for their source IPs for a short demo window.

alex_customer: DNS override is probably doable but needs approval (change control). Is there a cost for a test ENI? Also, our security team wants to know if Redwood supports client-side certs for mutual TLS for Private endpoints.

sara_sales: For POC we can provide a short-lived demo ENI at no extra charge; coordinate with support. We do support mutual TLS for Private in dedicated onboarding (needs cert exchange). I'll loop in reza for compliance answer.

eli_neteng: One more diagnostic request: please capture a short pcap of the TLS handshake from host A when it fails (tcpdump -w) and include the ClientHello bytes. We need to confirm whether SNI is present and what it's set to. Also run `iptables -t nat -L -n -v` on the host to check for any DNAT rules that could redirect to a local proxy.

alex_customer: Uploading pcap: https://files.corp.example/poc/pcap/1965432100.pcap - tcpdump shows ClientHello with SNI `redwood-poc.redwood.internal`. ServerHello from IP 10.5.200.7 has cert for `appliance.login.local`. I can also attach iptables output.

reza_security: Thanks. Two notes for customer security team:
1) If the appliance terminates TLS, they must approve that session termination for PII-sensitive traffic. We can provide a short data-flow diagram and attestations for POC scope.
2) Mutual TLS: yes, supported for Private endpoints. We'll need to exchange CA roots and finalize a CSR flow. That is a heavier lift than a DNS override.

mikael_support: I've opened ticket POC-4802 and linked to internal CC INC-2026-1989. Assigning to neteng + support. Status: triage.

support-bot: support-bot: Ticket POC-4802 created and linked to support rotation. Please add any additional logs to the ticket.

eli_neteng: If we want to be 100% sure it's the appliance, try: `curl --resolve redwood-poc.redwood.internal:443:<our-test-eni-ip> https://redwood-poc.redwood.internal` from the app host. That forces DNS without a resolver change. If that succeeds and returns our JSON, it's DNS/proxy interception.

alex_customer: Running that now... success! We get the expected JSON payload and TLS cert from Redwood. That proves the appliance is in the path.

sara_sales: Great info. Next steps:
- Alex: proceed with change control to add a DNS override OR ask proxy team to disable TLS-inspection for the FQDN.
- Redwood: will provision test ENI and provide exact IPs + short how-to for the `--resolve` workaround in case they need an immediate demo override.
- Security: reza will draft a short POC attestation for their compliance team about data handling during non-terminated TLS and mTLS options.

alex_customer: Will open the change request now. ETA 4 hours. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

mikael_support: Noted. I'll keep POC-4802 updated and mark the blocker until DNS/proxy change is complete. If the change is delayed we can enable the temporary public demo endpoint as a fallback.

reza_security: Also adding a checklist item for them to confirm appliance logs retention and whether they inspect request bodies for that hostname. We need explicit confirmation before moving to production.

sara_sales: Thanks everyone. Keeping this thread as the single place for demos/approvals. Alex, ping here when change control is approved and we'll flip the demo ENI. :thumbsup:
